economy.summary: Two busy weeks: the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island on Nov 3, Democrats won control of Congress in the Nov 3 midterms, and the S&P 500 fell 4.4% on Nov 5 before recovering to 7,562 by Nov 13. October consumer prices rose a hotter-than-expected 0.4%, the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.15%, and markets now price a December rate hike as near-certain. Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Nov 12. Next up: Nvidia and Home Depot (Nov 17), Disney (Nov 17), Walmart (Nov 19) and the Fed on Dec 8-9.
economy.fed: The Fed raised rates in September, then held at 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 in a 10-2 vote; the two dissenters wanted another hike. After the hot October CPI, futures price about an 87% chance of a quarter-point hike in December and a 13% chance of a half-point hike.
economy.fedNext: The next meeting is Dec 8-9. October CPI (released Nov 10) rose 0.4% for the month, above the 0.3% expected, with core up 0.3% for a third straight month; there is no annual figure because the 2025 shutdown skipped October 2025 data. Governor Waller said a half-point move should be on the table, and Dallas Fed President Logan wants two more quarter-point hikes. CME FedWatch puts the odds of a December hike near 100%.
economy.oil: The US-Iran war has largely shut the Strait of Hormuz since late February. After the US strike on Qeshm Island on Nov 3, US crude (WTI) touched $96, then fell to about $88.50 by Nov 13 as Qatar-mediated talks continued; Brent was near $99 on Nov 4.
sources: October CPI: energy prices hit consumers (Fox Business)
Hot inflation report raises odds of a jumbo hike (Yahoo Finance)
Dow rallies after Democratic midterm sweep (WBTV)
US self-defense strikes on Iran (CBS News)

GOOGL: Q3 revenue rose 25% to about $127.6B, slightly below estimates, and Google Cloud grew 103% to $30.7B. But adjusted EPS of $2.12 fell far short of the roughly $3.00 expected, free cash flow was negative $9.1B, Alphabet kept its 2026 capex plan at $195B–$205B, and Other Bets lost $20.4B. The stock fell 12.6% on Oct 29, its worst day since going public in 2004, wiping out roughly $500B of market value.
Alphabet heads for its biggest drop in market value (Yahoo Finance)
MSFT: Fiscal Q1 revenue rose 19% to $92.3B and adjusted EPS was $4.89, both above estimates. Azure grew 48%, beating Microsoft's own 44–45% forecast, to $33.2B; Microsoft Cloud reached $63.9B (up 30%); and the Q2 outlook calls for Azure growth of 49–50%. Capex of $45.2B came in below the roughly $50.7B expected. Shares rose about 4% after hours but slipped about 1% on Oct 29 as Alphabet's drop weighed on tech.
Azure beats Microsoft's own forecast again (Stock Titan)
AMZN: Q3 sales rose 12% to $201.9B and operating income hit $28.1B, a record 13.9% margin. AWS grew 39% to $46.0B, its fastest in nearly five years, with a $578B backlog, and Amazon said AWS can grow over 40% in both 2027 and 2028. But EPS of $1.89 came in under the roughly $1.97 expected, and its spending plans worried investors; the stock fell after hours and closed down 1.4% on Oct 30.
META: Q3 revenue rose 26% to $64.6B and Q4 is guided to $73B–$76B. But a $9.9B legal charge (a settlement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental-health claims) cut operating income 37%; without it, EPS would have been $7.40 instead of $3.83. Capital spending of $34.9B was more than the business brought in, so free cash flow was negative $2.1B, and Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex range (now $135B–$145B). It also plans a non-voting Class C share, handed out as a one-for-one stock dividend in January 2027. The stock fell 7% the next day. On Nov 9 the stock rose 5.1% after JPMorgan added it to its Analyst Focus List.
Meta sinks as free cash flow turns negative (CNBC)
Why is Meta stock going up (Trefis)
NVDA: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and board member, effective immediately, days after Nvidia opened an investigation into reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort (he admitted an affair). CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches; the FT reports Huang is discussing a comeback. The stock fell about 13% in the week to $162.85. Fiscal Q3 results come Nov 17: Nvidia guided about $108B of revenue and options price roughly a 10% move.
Jensen Huang resigns, Kress named interim CEO (TechCrunch)
Huang discusses comeback, FT reports (US News)
HOOD: Record Q3 revenue of $1.42B (up 12%) was a bit below the roughly $1.43B expected; adjusted EPS of $0.60 beat $0.55, while GAAP EPS fell 16% to $0.51. Trading revenue rose 19%, but crypto revenue fell 55%, and prediction-market contracts ($173M) brought in more than crypto ($120M). Gold subscribers hit a record 5.2 million. The stock fell 3.3% the next day.
SOFI: Record Q3: adjusted net revenue rose 44% to $1.37B, adjusted EBITDA rose 70% to $470M, net income was $241M ($0.18 a share, up from $0.11) and members grew 35% to 17.1 million. SoFi raised its 2026 outlook to about $5.04B in adjusted net revenue and $0.61 in EPS, and gave a first 2027 outlook of about $6.4B in revenue and $0.90 in EPS. The stock rose about 18% in the two days after the report.
UNH: Q3 beat (adjusted EPS $4.69 vs. $4.15 expected) and 2026 guidance was raised to at least $20.50 per share.
TSLA: Tesla fell about 11% on Nov 5 as the midterm results clouded its data-center and SpaceX-merger outlook. On Nov 6 shareholders approved Elon Musk's new pay plan, which targets an $8.5 trillion valuation, and on Nov 9 the stock rose 5.5% as Tesla said robotaxi rides start in San Antonio this week. In Q3 (reported Oct 21): Q3 revenue was flat at $28.1B, but gross margin improved to 19.6% (from 18.0% a year ago) and adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.45 estimate. GAAP net income fell 43% to $787M, the operating margin was just 2.6%, energy revenue fell 16%, and free cash flow was $1.5B (vs. $4.0B a year ago). Tesla said its robotaxis have driven nearly 2 million unsupervised miles. The stock fell 3% the day after the report, then jumped 5% on Oct 26.
What triggered the move in Tesla stock (Trefis)
Q3 beat on margins and cash flow (investinglive)
NFLX: Q3 EPS of $0.87 beat the $0.82 estimate and revenue of $12.9B (up 12%) matched, with a 34.6% operating margin. But Q4 revenue guidance of $13.4B came in under the $13.5B expected, and Netflix cut its 2026 ad revenue forecast to about $2.7B from $3B, citing a slower rollout of some ad features. The stock fell 5% the next day and closed at $63.90 on Oct 26, down 32% this year.
Why Netflix fell despite the beat (Finviz)
CRWD: Rose about 15% from Oct 19 to Oct 26 as cybersecurity stocks rallied on worries about a wave of AI-enabled cyberattacks. CrowdStrike also expanded its partnership with Nvidia to build security in at the chip level, and Mizuho raised its price target to $275. The stock has more than doubled this year.
NOW: Q3 revenue of about $4.11B was roughly as expected, but adjusted EPS of $1.00 missed $1.02, subscription gross margin fell to 80% from 83%, and ServiceNow guided Q4 growth in contracted revenue (cRPO) to about 18.5%, down from 20.5%. That revived fears that AI will slow software sales, and the stock fell 26.9% on Oct 29, its worst day in over 14 years. ServiceNow raised its AI contract target to $1.7B, and some analysts called the drop an overreaction.
KO: Q3 EPS of $0.91 and revenue of $13.4B beat estimates, and Coca-Cola raised its full-year outlook to about 11% earnings growth. Shares dipped anyway on slowing demand in North America, after a record close on Oct 22; the stock is up about 33% this year.
Coca-Cola pulls back on slowing U.S. demand (Schaeffer's)
BA: Q3 revenue of $24.2B came in slightly above forecasts, but the core loss of $0.34 a share was wider than analysts expected (GAAP loss: $0.26). Free cash flow was positive at $0.5B, the order backlog hit a record $745B, and Boeing delivered 161 commercial jets in the quarter.
PYPL: Q3 adjusted EPS rose 8% to $1.45, well above the roughly $1.31 expected, but revenue grew only 2% to $8.6B, a bit short of forecasts. GAAP EPS fell 4% to $1.25.
NKE: Fiscal Q1 beat on profit (adjusted EPS $0.48 vs. $0.44 expected), but revenue fell 4% to $11.2B, Greater China sales fell 22%, and Nike now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to fall by a high-single-digit percentage with EPS of $1.15 to $1.35 (Wall Street had about $1.67). It also launched a $2.5B cost-savings plan.
JPM: Q3 profit rose 6% to $15.3B and revenue rose 8% to $50.2B, but adjusted EPS of $5.75 missed estimates near $5.85. Equity trading jumped 49%, buybacks were cut 84% from Q2, and the full-year net interest income outlook was raised to about $106B.
TSM: October revenue hit a record NT$586.9B, up 59.7% from a year earlier and 14.7% from September, on AI and 2-nanometer demand. January-October sales are up 43.3%. October alone is about a third of TSMC's US$52.3B-$54.3B Q4 guide. In Q3 (reported Oct 15): Q3 revenue of $46.7B (up 41%) beat the top of its own guidance; EPS rose 69% with a 58.7% operating margin. TSMC guided Q4 revenue to $52.3B to $54.3B (about 58% growth) and now expects 2026 revenue to grow about 44%.
ASML: Record Q3 sales of 11.7B euros with a 57.5% gross margin. ASML guided Q4 sales to 14.2B to 15.2B euros and full-year 2026 to 44B to 45B euros, saying customers raised equipment plans because of AI.
LLY: Q3 revenue of $24.4B and adjusted EPS of $7.48 beat estimates on strong demand for its GLP-1 drugs, and Lilly raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $91B–$92B. The stock rose about 6% on Oct 29.
Lilly pops on GLP-1 demand (Yahoo Finance)
VRT: Q3 revenue rose 61% to $4.31B and adjusted EPS of $2.21 beat estimates; Vertiv raised its full-year outlook. The stock jumped 16.5% on Oct 28.
Vertiv soars, GE Vernova slips (24/7 Wall St.)
GEV: Q3 revenue rose 27% to $12.64B and adjusted EPS of $4.81 beat estimates; the order backlog hit a record $197B and GE Vernova agreed to a $9B deal for Trench Group. The stock dipped about 6% at first but recovered most of the drop.
GE Vernova falls despite beat and raise (24/7 Wall St.)
INTC: Intel kept swinging with chip stocks after its Q3 drop: it fell 10.3% on Nov 5 in the post-election sell-off, then rose 7.7% on Nov 6 and 5.5% on Nov 9, with no company news. It is down about 54% since Oct 7. In Q3 (reported Oct 29), revenue grew 21% but a weak Q4 outlook and a $300M plant-shutdown charge sent the stock down 29%.
What just happened to Intel stock (Trefis)
COIN: Crypto stayed weak after Coinbase's soft Q3: over $1B of leveraged long bets were liquidated in the 24 hours to Nov 8, US spot bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.28B of outflows from Nov 2 to 6, and bitcoin slipped to about $75,000. The stock was about $132 on Nov 10. In Q3 (reported Oct 29): Q3 revenue fell about 35% to $1.20B, below the $1.23B expected, as crypto trading slowed; net income still rose 66% to $719M ($2.51 a share) thanks to gains on the crypto Coinbase holds. The stock fell 10.6% on Oct 30.
Bitcoin battles $1 billion of liquidations (Interactive Crypto)
V: Fiscal Q4 net revenue rose 13% to $12.1B and adjusted EPS was $3.48; full-year revenue grew 15% to $45.9B. Visa raised its quarterly dividend 16% to $0.78. The stock was little changed the next day and rose 2.5% on Oct 29.
XOM: Q3 adjusted EPS of $4.23 beat the $4.12 estimate and operating cash flow was $25.7B. Exxon announced $20B of buybacks for 2027 and a 4% dividend raise, its 44th straight yearly increase; strong refining offset lower oil-production earnings. The stock rose 2.2% on Oct 30.
MCD: Global comparable sales rose 1.5%, but US comps fell 0.2% (better than the -0.5% feared) on weak traffic, and international markets grew 1.4% versus 2.1% expected. Adjusted EPS of $3.57 beat, while revenue of $7.16B missed the $7.29B consensus. Management does not expect US results to improve in Q4 and cut its 2026 gross opening target to 2,500 restaurants from 2,600.
US same-store sales decline on weak traffic (Nation's Restaurant News)
UBER: Q3 revenue rose about 10% to $14.8B, in line, and gross bookings grew 20% to $59.8B. Adjusted EPS of $0.88 edged past estimates, but GAAP EPS was only $0.25 because of a $476M loss on equity investments. Uber guided Q4 bookings to $63.25B-$65.25B and adjusted EBITDA to $2.41B-$2.51B, slightly below the $2.49B estimate, and the stock slipped.
Uber delivers solid earnings, tepid guidance (Stocktwits)
VST: Adjusted EPS of $3.23 beat the $2.94 estimate, though revenue of $6.35B missed. Vistra narrowed 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $7.1B-$7.5B with a higher midpoint, set 2027 guidance at $7.7B-$8.5B of EBITDA and $4.3B-$5.1B of free cash flow, closed the Cogentrix deal and authorized another $1.5B of buybacks (about $2.5B remaining).
Vistra Q3 earnings beat on power pricing (Zacks)
AAPL: Fiscal Q4 revenue rose 12% to a September-quarter record $114.5B and EPS was $2.10 ($2.05 excluding tariff refunds) versus about $1.98 expected. iPhone revenue grew about 17% to $57.6B and Services hit a record $31.6B. Apple guided December-quarter revenue up 7-10%, which it called the best quarter in its history, but iPhone Duo deliveries slip into 2027 in some cases and the 45-46% gross margin guide disappointed; the stock fell about 4%.
AVGO: Broadcom swung with the AI trade: it fell 10.4% on Nov 5 in the post-election chip sell-off, then jumped 8.8% on Nov 9 with no company news. Fiscal Q4 results come Dec 10.
AMD: Q3 revenue rose 45% to a record $13.4B, above AMD's own $12.7B-$13.3B range, with data center revenue up 97% to $8.5B (server CPUs +103%, Instinct GPUs +98% on the MI450 launch). Adjusted EPS was $2.09, up 74%. AMD guided Q4 revenue to about $17B (plus or minus 3%), roughly 66% growth, with gross margin near 55%. The stock rose about 5% after hours; analysts flagged a large inventory build weighing on cash flow.
AMD record Q3 as data center rises 97% (Let's Data Science)
MU: Micron rose about 13% in the week to $778 after TrendForce forecast higher Q4 DRAM and NAND contract prices, recovering part of its early-November slide. Fiscal Q1 2027 results are expected around Dec 16.
Weekly market review, Nov 13 (The Glass Desk)
PLTR: Q3 revenue of $2.31B beat the $2.17B forecast and adjusted EPS of $0.44 beat $0.41. Palantir raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $8.530B-$8.534B. The stock still fell about 3% the next day and more after hours, as analysts pointed to order backlog that was flat from the prior quarter and investors grew choosier about AI stocks.
NBIS: Q3 revenue of about $981M (up roughly 571%) beat the $907.5M estimate, but Nebius said delays at partner data centers put its 2026 revenue at the low end of its forecast range. Reported backlog barely grew from June. The stock fell about 16% to around $131.
Nebius beats Q3 estimates, shares fall on delays (StockAnalysis)
COST: October net sales rose 12.6% to $24.5B. Comparable sales excluding gas and currency rose 7.3% (US 8.1%), and digital sales grew 22.5%. Higher gas prices added about 4 points to reported comps.
CEG: Adjusted operating EPS of $5.06 beat the $3.89 estimate (a year ago: $3.04) and revenue rose about 45% to $9.55B with Calpine included. Constellation raised 2026 guidance to $12.50-$12.80 from $11.50-$12.50, agreed to buy the Rhode Island State Energy Center for $715M and got a conditional loan commitment of up to $5B. It will give 2027-2028 guidance and a growth outlook to 2030 with year-end results.
Constellation raises 2026 outlook after Q3 beat (Stocktwits)
OKLO: Q3 revenue was about $1.9M and the operating loss doubled to $71M; cash and securities were about $3.1B. Oklo now frames its first Aurora powerhouse as a 2028-2029 start instead of 2028, and a PJM setback added to the timeline worries. It did win approval for a new fuel facility.
Oklo Q3 2026 results and business update (Finviz)
Oklo narrows loss but Aurora slips (Finviz)
SPCX: Q3 revenue rose 161% to $14.6B, beating the roughly $12.7B consensus, and net income was $4.4B versus a $1.1B loss a year ago. The AI unit brought in $7.56B and Starlink-led connectivity $5.25B (+69%, about 13.6M subscribers). Capex was $19.6B. SpaceX expects Q1 2027 revenue of $33B-$37B. The stock fell 9% on Nov 5 on midterm regulation worries, then recovered to about $143 by Nov 10.
SpaceX stock falls 9% on midterm worries (Gotrade)
ARM: Fiscal Q2 revenue rose 27% to a record $1.44B and adjusted EPS of $0.52 beat forecasts. Arm raised its AGI CPU revenue outlook to up to $2B across fiscal 2027-2028, but royalty growth slowed sharply, annualized contract value was a bit light and Q3 guidance (EPS $0.52-$0.60) only matched estimates. The stock fell about 5% after hours.
Arm shares fall despite Q2 beat (investingLive)
IONQ: Q3 revenue rose 336% to $173.8M versus $141M expected, and IonQ raised 2026 revenue guidance to $505M-$515M. Remaining performance obligations doubled to $1.2B. The operating loss was about $433M; GAAP net income of $564M came only from a non-cash warrant gain. IonQ also agreed to buy security firm Elisity for $1.15B in stock. The stock rose about 23% the next day.
IonQ record Q3 and raised guidance (IonQ)
Why IonQ stock is soaring (Motley Fool)
RKLB: Q3 revenue rose 73% to a record $268M and backlog reached about $3.6B, but the loss of $0.12 a share was wider than the $0.07 expected. A propellant-tank defect pushed Neutron's first launch to no earlier than 2027, though eight Neutron missions were booked at a new $70M base price. Q4 revenue is guided to $270M-$290M; liquidity is about $4.7B. The stock fell about 5% after hours.
Rocket Lab falls after Q3 miss despite record backlog (Finviz)
Rocket Lab Q3 earnings call highlights (MarketBeat)
SHOP: Revenue grew 32% to about $3.7B, ahead of Shopify's own low-30s guide, and adjusted EPS of $0.49 beat. But GMV of about $119B missed the $120B estimate and subscription revenue of $836M missed $850M. AI-referred orders rose 3.3x. The stock closed down about 9%.
Why Shopify stock dove today (Motley Fool)
BRK.B: Q3 operating earnings fell 5.8% to $12.7B as insurance underwriting profit dropped 43%, while BNSF rose 19%. Berkshire bought back $9.6B of its own stock, more than double the prior quarter. Its cash and Treasury bills dipped to $352B from $359B in June.
CPNG: Revenue rose 7% (11% in constant currency) to $10.0B, above the $9.75B estimate, but Coupang posted a $450M operating loss and a $501M net loss as an Incheon fulfillment-center fire, data-incident costs and customer discounts hit margins. Free cash flow was -$72M. It guided Q4 constant-currency growth of 13-14% and expects margins to recover by mid-2027.
